result.coreDiagnosis: The candidate's resume exhibits a pattern of extremely short tenures across multiple roles (average ~9 months), coupled with a majority of experience at the 'Associate Product Manager' level, which significantly undermines the expectation for sustained, end-to-end product ownership required for a mid-level Product Manager (Technical).
result.roleFitVerdict: While demonstrating strong feature-level impact and technical fluency with AI/LLM, the candidate's job hopping and limited tenure at the 'Product Manager' title band suggest a poor fit for the sustained, strategic ownership expected of a 3-5 year mid-level PM (Technical).
recruiterScan: (Tenure) Significant job hopping: 4 roles in ~3 years 1 month, with the longest tenure being 1 year 8 months.
(Level) Predominantly Associate PM roles; only 8 months as 'Product Manager' at current role.
(Stack) Credible LLM/AI technical fluency with prompt engineering and API usage for PM(T).
(Impact) Strong, quantified feature-level outcomes and metrics across recent roles.
(Risk) '5+ Years' claim in summary does not align with explicit work history (~3 years 1 month).

topHiringRisks.title: Lack of Sustained Ownership
topHiringRisks.description: The pattern of very short tenures (4-8 months at 3/4 roles) indicates a lack of experience seeing product initiatives through multiple phases (discovery, launch, iteration, scaling, sunset), which is critical for a mid-level PM owning a product area.

topHiringRisks.title: Level Mismatch (Experience Band)
topHiringRisks.description: While individual bullet points show strong impact, the majority of experience is at the 'Associate Product Manager' level, and the total explicit experience is closer to 3 years, not a solid 3-5 years of mid-level PM experience. The current 'Product Manager' tenure is too short to validate the jump.

topHiringRisks.title: Stability/Retention Risk
topHiringRisks.description: The consistent pattern of short stays (4, 5, 8 months) suggests a high risk of the candidate leaving within a year, which is a significant investment risk for any company, especially for a PM role that requires deep domain knowledge over time.
